precepts.text: How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger! The beauty of Israel. So we were cast down to the earth, meaning we were brought down low, we were brought into captivity, we were not on top ruling any more. So this is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.
precepts.point: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. It is talking about a place of authority. When you read the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise. Then there is heaven which is the sky and space. And then there are heavens like a place of authority.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

precepts.text: All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem. The other nations is happy that we thrown down, happy that we at the bottom. Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth? Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty, and even in the lowest state we in, everything we do, everybody follows us. All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: you see it in the stores and shops in our own neighborhoods; they don't regard us. They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for. We don't have a community; in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. But now the Lord is waking his people back up to get his people back in order, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.
precepts.point: Yet we have not hearkened unto his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he hath set before us. We crying out to our people day and night on all these different platforms and radio shows, and our people still will not wake up, like them brothers we sat down with, still fighting against it to this day.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
Baruch says, “Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God”, and “unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.” Here in America we have open shame, because we departed from our God and refuse to come back and repent. Lamentations shows what that open shame looks like.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

precepts.text: The Lord cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel: heaven is dominion and rulership, the high estate, and we were set down to a low state.
precepts.point: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man? Not, is this the fallen angel; not the Nephilim. Is this the man that made the earth to tremble? What man made the earth to tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere? He's the man, the oppressor, the king of Babylon that we read about in this chapter. It is not going into some angel, because all the angels take their directive from the Most High God.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”: before we can know who Lucifer is, we have to know what heaven is. Lamentations shows it: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.”

Heaven is dominion and rulership. That was the high standard, the high estate Israel held, and the beauty of Israel was cast down from it to the earth. We were set down to a low state. No one thinks Israel was literally thrown out of the sky; we fell from rulership.

So it is with Lucifer. Esau takes Jude and Isaiah 14, mixes them up and comes with this fallen angel teaching. But keep it in context. Lucifer, the lightbearer, is the king of Babylon of verse 4, the oppressor, the one who “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke.” It is talking about a nation: this so-called white man, America, whom everybody looks at as god and all knowing because he controls communication everywhere.

He is falling from heaven the same way Israel did: he is losing his dominion and his rulership. “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: not a fallen angel, not the Nephilim, but the man, the one who made the earth tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere. The angels are not falling out of heaven; they take their directive from the Most High God.

precepts.text: The Lord cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, from rulership to servitude, because we went away from the author who created us and looked to another nation for beauty. America under the skirt is a worn-out harlot who has been with everyone on the block. Knowing that, we return.
precepts.point: I will surely avenge them; my people is led as a flock to the slaughter; I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt, but bring them out with a mighty hand and smite Egypt with plagues as before and destroy all the land thereof. As before means a coming Egypt, the United States. When it comes, we do not want to go down with it.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The Lord likened the daughter of Zion to a comely woman, yet Jeremiah laments: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!”

The Lord cast the beauty of Israel down from heaven, from rulership, to the earth, to servitude. Why would he do that? Because we went off. We went away from the author who created us. That is why you would look to another nation for its beauty.

But God is letting you know he is the author, the creator of beauty. And America, that you think is beautiful, really is not beautiful. Under the skirt she is a worn-out harlot: you think she is beautiful, then you realize she has been with everyone on the block.

You went against your God. So now, knowing that, we have to return. We have to return back to the author of our beauty, so that he will avenge us and bring us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

precepts.text: What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee? A breach is a split or a tear, and the root of reparations is repair. Isaiah 58:11-12: the Lord shall guide thee continually and satisfy thy soul in drought; they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places, and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in. Our souls in drought will be watered and healed.
precepts.point: Sin is the transgression of the law, 1 John 3:4. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: those under the law break it and are under sin, and both Jews and Gentiles under sin means both under the law, which the other nations never were. That every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God, the world that received God's commandments under Moses. Therefore by the deeds of the law, sacrifice, there shall no flesh be justified in his sight, for we are justified by Christ's blood; for by the law is the knowledge of sin, because to acknowledge a sin, willful or ignorant, you had to bring an animal.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul proves from the Psalms that Israel became filthy: “They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” The whole nation was broken. Jeremiah laments that same breaking: “What thing shall I liken to thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? what shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Zion? for thy breach is great like the sea: who can heal thee?”

A breach is a split or a tear. Our breach is great like the sea. Who can heal us? Christ, our saviour.

Isaiah shows the healing: “And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.” When our souls are in drought, the Lord is going to water us and heal us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”, the waste places we made when we became filthy. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.”

The root word of reparations is repair. The repairer of the breach: that is the reparations right there. Both Jews and Gentiles, Judah and Ephraim, were “all under sin” and torn apart, and the one who heals that breach is Christ, repairing and restoring Israel.

precepts.text: All that pass by clap their hands, hiss, and wag their head, asking is this the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth.
precepts.point: The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.” Jeremiah saw it done: “All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?”

The wagging of the head is the shaking of the head among the people. We were the perfection of beauty and the joy of the whole earth, and we became an astonishment: put into slavery, our names changed, our culture and lands taken, and another nation took our name. So the nations clap their hands and hiss and ask, is this them?

precepts.text: The Most High cast down the beauty of Israel from heaven to the earth, out of rulership; we have been scattered to the four corners.
precepts.point: Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy holy spirit from me. The best thing going for us is to be in the presence of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 51: Acknowledge, Repent, and Be Cleansed

precepts.why:
“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger!” The Most High cast down the beauty of Israel from heaven to the earth, out of rulership. We have been scattered to the four corners.

That is what it looks like to be cast away from his presence. David asks the Most High not to do to him what was done to the daughter of Zion. Being in the presence of the Most High is the best thing going for us, and losing it is losing everything.

precepts.text: Ezra testified the law was burnt, so the Most High put His spirit on Ezra and other men to rewrite the torah.
precepts.point: When the enemy entered the sanctuary and burned everything, they burned our torahs, records, and scrolls, which is why the law is said to be no more.

note.label: Lamentations 2: The Most High Turned Enemy Against Zion

precepts.why:
Her king and princes are among the Gentiles, “the law is no more; her prophets also find no vision from the Lord.” How is the law no more? When the enemy entered the sanctuary and burned everything, they burned our torahs, records, and scrolls.

Ezra testified to it: “For thy law is burnt, therefore no man knoweth the things that are done of thee, or the work that shall begin.” Because the law was burnt, the Most High put His spirit on Ezra and other men to rewrite the torah. That is why Lamentations can say the law is no more, with the sanctuary abhorred, the solemn feasts and sabbaths forgotten in Zion, and the king and princes among the Gentiles.

precepts.text: The Most High cast down from heaven to the earth the beauty of Israel, cast down from rulership.
precepts.point: The sheet was let down from heaven by four corners, meaning Israel was cast down from a position of rulership to the earth into servitude, to be gathered again from the four corners as the outcasts of Israel.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
The sheet was “let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me.”

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” Let down from heaven means Israel was cast down from a position of rulership to the earth, into servitude. The beauty of Israel was brought down, and that is what Peter saw let down before him.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why: The Israelites explain this fall from heaven. “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel,” So he cast the Israelites down from heaven. Does that mean we were flying in the sky? No, it does not. It means we were at one time the top nation on earth, and we fell to hell, meaning captivity, a low estate. So when Isaiah 14:12 says how art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, it is in the same context: your friendly neighborhood white man is going to fall from heaven.

moments.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

points: Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee: the prophets he's talking about are the hirelings, these hireling pastors, these hireling Israelites. You could count down the vain and foolish things they've seen: there's going to be peace, there's going to be love, you can marry white women, you could have 15 wives while you're in the midst of poverty and God accepts all that. Lie, lie, lie. Give your tithe, give your 10% of your check every week. Let me lay hands on you, Sister Betty; God wants me to rub all over you. Lie, lie, lie.

And they have not discovered thine iniquity: they never said, hey, the reason blacks and Latinos are in captivity or suffer from oppression is because you break God's commandments. They never tell us that. They said, this is your season, God is going to bless you; if you donate $1,000 to me, you're going to get 10,000 by the end of the year. That's all lies.
To turn away thy captivity: Christ died on the cross to save us from our sins, cuz we went in captivity because of our sins. That's why Christ had to come.

But have seen for thee false burdens and causes of banishment. A false burden is something you don't have to carry, but you carry it anyway. Like Christmas: people spend all their money, all their check on Christmas gifts; it's a waste of time. Easter: you got to get a new suit every Easter, new shoes, new socks, new drawers too. New Year's Eve, wedding anniversaries, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving: it's a false burden, cuz no way that God said, oh, today is my birthday, what are you going to buy me? So by us supporting those false burdens, it causes us to be banished from the coming kingdom. We're banished from New Jerusalem.

You can't equal anything to what we went through. Slavery, the transatlantic slave trade, was the worst crime in history, and only the Most High God can heal us from what it did to us.
